inference: Keep scratch arrays in ordinary owned Vecs, and introduce shared storage only for reads from an immutable retained payload. A write unwraps or copies a retained buffer into an owned Vec, without allocating a new shared header. Publishing an owned array still copies it into a retained Arc and can cost more than baseline.
ownership: The two-form scratch storage is private: Owned(Vec) or Retained(Arc<Vec>). Cloning owned scratch preserves the original deep Vec copy; cloning a retained read shares rational data. Closed storage exposes only immutable reads and conversion to a scratch view. Empty retained storage is None. Polynomial terms and opaque Computable owners keep their original Vec behavior.
publication_and_release: Closed conversion first rejects every opaque atom, then copies owned arrays or shares already-retained arrays. The original cache publication and lock scope are unchanged. Exclusive writable access first converts the only non-owned variant before returning a mutable Vec; its unreachable arm is a private construction invariant, not a numeric-domain path. Unique retained buffers can be unwrapped after the cache owner is dropped; shared buffers are copied before mutation or consumption.
cost_risk: Owned publication adds an Arc allocation. The scratch enum may enlarge coefficients, even while closed coefficients shrink. Retained reads can avoid copies, but borrowed-to-owned transitions, first-query costs, stack/heap layouts and binary size must all be measured. The prior rejected version is not the new baseline and its samples are not extended.

alias_control_change.meaning: Only the pointer-inventory observation changes.
